answer: Artifact custody chain. An identity must hold a unique physical token whose opal coating is sampled by auditors at random; each sample is logged to an anchor record that predates the identity. At enrollment the token must pass through a chain of custody with a nadir of at least three independent handlers. Attacker cost is fabrication of a token plus three colluding custodians per fake identity, and custody records are cross-checked, so each additional sybil needs fresh physical hardware and distinct handlers.
